specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** ephesus-sites-evidence-judge
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge the strength of the evidence for ten claims about the Christian sites of Ephesus and Selçuk, rating each as documented, debated, or tradition only, with at least 8 of 10 correct and the reason chosen for each. **Prerequisites:** primary source and myth versus history (Chapter 4); the Book of Acts and Paul in Ephesus (Chapter 9); the Church of Mary at Ephesus, the Council of Ephesus, John the Apostle, the Basilica of St. John, the House of the Virgin Mary, St. Paul's Prison Tower, and the riot of the silversmiths (all defined in this chapter above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of ten claim cards, the learner chooses one rating and then one of two reasons. A card is correct when both the rating and the reason match the Content. Mastery is 8 of 10 cards correct on the first attempt. **Misconceptions:** (1) A real ancient building proves the story attached to it (cards 3, 5, 8). (2) "Tradition" means "false" (card 9). (3) If a holy site is visited by popes, its identification has been proven (card 8). (4) Everything in Acts is either proven or invented, with nothing in between (cards 6, 7). **Instructional Rationale:** Rating evidence against stated criteria is an Evaluate task: the learner must weigh the kind and age of the evidence, not just recall a fact. Requiring a reason after each rating makes the learner justify the judgment, and separating the building from the story attached to it targets the most common confusion at religious sites. **Content:** Ratings, with the definition shown: - **Documented:** contemporary or near-contemporary written or archaeological evidence supports it. - **Debated:** some early evidence supports it, but scholars disagree about whether it is reliable. - **Tradition only:** first recorded long after the events, with no early evidence for or against. Reasons offered (two per card, one correct): | # | Claim shown to the learner | Correct rating | Correct reason | Wrong reason offered | Feedback | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | The Council of Ephesus met in the Church of Mary in 431 CE. | Documented | The council's own records name the church. | Guides have always said so. | The acts of the council, written at the time, place it in the church called Mary. | | 2 | Justinian built a great domed basilica on the hill of Ayasuluk. | Documented | Procopius, writing in Justinian's reign, describes it, and the ruins match. | It is the largest ruin in Selçuk. | A contemporary author and the excavated building agree. | | 3 | The tower on Bülbül Dağı was a prison where Paul was held. | Tradition only | The tower is a Hellenistic wall tower; no early source links it to Paul. | Acts describes Paul's imprisonment in this tower. | Acts mentions no imprisonment in Ephesus; the name is a later local tradition. | | 4 | The tower on Bülbül Dağı was part of the city wall of Lysimachus. | Documented | Its masonry and its position on the line of the wall date it to the early 3rd century BCE. | Paul was imprisoned there. | The building itself is securely dated; only its name is tradition. | | 5 | John the Apostle is buried beneath the Basilica of St. John. | Tradition only | The earliest written claim, about 190 CE, comes about a century after his death. | A tomb is marked beneath the dome. | A marked tomb shows what pilgrims believed, not who lies there. | | 6 | John the Apostle lived at Ephesus in his old age. | Debated | Irenaeus (about 180 CE) says so, but scholars dispute which John he meant. | No ancient writer mentions it. | The tradition is early and local, and scholars still argue over how reliable it is. | | 7 | Silversmiths rioted in the theater of Ephesus against Paul. | Debated | Only Acts tells it, written a generation later, though its local details fit the city. | Inscriptions record the riot. | No inscription records the riot; Acts' accurate local detail makes it plausible but not proven. | | 8 | Mary, the mother of Jesus, lived her last years in the house on Bülbül Dağı. | Tradition only | The identification comes from 19th-century visions; the chapel is mostly Byzantine. | Three popes have visited it. | Papal visits honor the pilgrimage; the Church has not ruled on the identification. | | 9 | The chapel on Bülbül Dağı is a place where Christians and Muslims pray today. | Documented | Visitors of both faiths can be seen praying there now. | The chapel's identification is unproven, so it is not a real holy place. | Whatever its history, its present role as a shared place of prayer is a plain fact. | | 10 | Paul spent two to three years based in Ephesus. | Documented | Paul's own letters, written from Ephesus, and Acts both place him there. | The Basilica of St. John honors him. | Paul's letters are primary sources; 1 Corinthians was written from Ephesus. | Answer counts: Documented 5, Debated 2, Tradition only 3. **Provenance:** Claims, ratings, and reasons from this chapter's sections "The Church of Mary at Ephesus," "The Council of Ephesus," "John the Apostle," "The Basilica of St. John," "The House of the Virgin Mary," "St. Paul's Prison Tower," and "The Riot of the Silversmiths," and from Chapter 9's "Paul in Ephesus." **Rules:** - Ten cards in the fixed order listed; the two reasons for each card appear in random order. - The learner first chooses a rating, then a reason. A card is correct only if both match. - One attempt per card. Score 0 to 10; mastery is score >= 8. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the three rating definitions. 2. A claim card appears; the learner chooses a rating. 3. Two reasons appear; the learner chooses one. 4. Feedback appears, and the card joins a summary column under its correct rating. 5. After card 10, the learner sees the score and the three columns. 6. The learner should notice that cards 3 and 4 are about the same tower and get different ratings, because the building and the story attached to it are separate claims. **Feedback:** Correct (rating and reason): "Correct. [Feedback]" Correct rating with wrong reason: "Right rating, but look again at why: [Feedback]" Wrong rating: "This one is [correct rating]. [Feedback]" For a wrong answer on card 9, add "Tradition about the past does not change what happens there today." After card 10: "You judged [n] of 10. Mastery is 8." If n < 8, a "Judge again" option restarts from card 1. **Starting State:** Three empty columns labeled Documented, Debated, and Tradition only, card 1 showing, and the question "How strong is the evidence?" **Chapter Anchors:** Council of Ephesus 431 CE in the Church of Mary; Justinian's basilica described by Procopius; Lysimachus' wall early 3rd century BCE; Irenaeus about 180 CE; Polycrates about 190 CE; Anne Catherine Emmerich's visions published 1852; three papal visits; ten cards; mastery 8 of 10.
